text.p: Violence escalated near the Israel-Lebanon border overnight. Arab guerrillas set off a roadside bomb and fired mortar rounds. Israeli forces retaliated with an air attack.
Military sources said at least one pro-Israeli militiaman was killed when the bomb exploded in south Lebanon late on Wednesday.
Israeli army radio said an Arab guerrilla was also killed in fighting overnight but this could not be immediately confirmed.

The bomb exploded in the Jezzine area just outside Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone, the sources said. It killed a pro-Israeli South Lebanon Army (SLA) militiaman and lightly wounded three, the sources said.

In Beirut, the pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) claimed responsibility for the roadside bomb. SLA sources said the explosion prompted retaliatory Israeli shelling north of Jezzine in south Lebanon.
Army radio said Israeli troops killed the guerrilla in fighting in the northeastern sector of the occupation zone. The army said its warplanes also struck a guerrilla target in southern Lebanon.

The mortar rounds fired from Lebanon exploded on both sides of the border before dawn on Thursday, injuring no one, Israeli military sources said. They said the rounds were apparently aimed at troops and not northern Israeli residents.

The 3,000-strong SLA militia helps some 1,000 Israeli troops hold a 15-km (nine-mile)-deep zone in south Lebanon to guard northern Israel from guerrilla attacks. Hizbollah aims to drive the Israelis out.
The rise in tensions on Israel's northern front followed a day of Israeli-Palestinian unrest in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

Israeli troops, coming under a rain of petrol bombs and rocks, fired rubber-coated metal bullets and wounded 37 Palestinians in the divided West Bank town of Hebron, witnesses said. Soldiers shot dead an Arab teenager in a clash in Gaza.
Israel warned the Palestinian Authority to quell the violence or risk a stronger military response.
